episodes.208278: A strong upper-level storm system tracked through the eastern portion of the United States on December 18, 2025. A very strong jet and potent cold front was associated with this system. As it neared Middle Tennessee, southerly winds strengthened ahead of it during the afternoon hours and continued to strengthen as the cold front and a line of showers with isolated thunderstorms swept east through the area. Wind gusts of 35 to 45 mph were common with some sporadic wind gusts over 50 mph with these showers. This caused several reports of downed trees, mainly across central portions of Middle Tennessee. Meanwhile, one particular thunderstorm strengthened as it moved through Warren County. It caused a swath of damaging straight-line winds near McMinnville which caused tree and structural damage there.
episodes.208309: A strong storm system passing to the north of central Indiana on the 18th produced strong gradient wind gusts up to 30-40 mph.  Late day convective showers with the associated cold front included an embedded thin line of strongly-forced heavier rain.  While poor lapse rates and negligible instability below the -20 degree Celsius level prevented any thunder, the line did produce brief marginally severe winds in Hendricks County that collapsed an old and partially-compromised grain bin southwest of Clayton.  An NWS survey determined no tornado occurred at this location.
episodes.208324: A line of strong thunderstorms moved across the coastal waters ahead of a cold front.  A couple of gusts in excess of 34 knots were measured.
episodes.209376: A robust cold front pushed across Illinois during the late morning, with a narrow line of showers and thunderstorms present along the front. This line of storms produced a few instances of wind damage west of the I-55 corridor.
episodes.209409: A thin line of thunderstorms caused isolated thunderstorm wind damage in west-central Illinois.

events.narrative: An empty semi-truck was tipped over on Route 24 northeast of Rushville.
Thunderstorm winds downed numerous power poles down along US 67 on the north side of Carrollton.
Power lines were blown down on Jacobs Road between Manito and Green Valley.
